name: Deficit Handstand Push-Up
description: The deficit handstand push-up places the hands on elevated surfaces (parallettes, blocks, or plates) to allow the head to descend below hand level, dramatically increasing the range of motion compared to a standard wall HSPU. The greater depth significantly increases the stretch placed on the anterior deltoid and upper pectoralis, and demands substantially more shoulder strength and stability through the extended range.

execution.starting_position: Place parallettes, yoga blocks, or stable elevated surfaces at appropriate hand positions. Kick to a handstand against a wall with hands on the elevated surface. Hands at shoulder width or slightly wider.
execution.setup_instructions: Elevation of 10-20 cm is a typical starting deficit. Ensure the elevated surfaces are stable and non-slip before loading.
steps: Step 1: Kick up to a handstand with hands on elevated surfaces.
Step 2: Lower the head below hand level — the degree of descent depends on the elevation height.
Step 3: Hold the bottom position briefly if training strength.
Step 4: Press back to full arm extension.
Step 5: Maintain rigid body position — no arch or piked hips.
common_mistakes: Attempting too large a deficit before the standard HSPU is mastered
Instability in the elevated surface — safety first
safety_considerations: Prerequisites: 10+ clean wall HSPUs before adding a deficit
Start with a small deficit (5-10 cm) and progress gradually
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension to head below hand level.
coaching_cues: Let the head descend below the hands
Press all the way to full arm extension
Body stays straight — no hip pike
